headline: Budget committee holds first community meeting and takes public testimony

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: Speakers, limited to three minutes each, addressed bus service, STEM programs, transitional housing, deer damage to farmland and farm funding. The chair said the committee will receive a summary of the testimony.
meeting.recap: The Budget, Finance and Economic Development Committee held its first community meeting and plans to visit every district.[[0:00:00]] The agenda had one item, and each speaker could talk for up to three minutes.[[0:01:36]] A bus rider said the bus service makes part-time work possible.[[0:03:28]] A fifth grader asked the council to keep and increase funding for MEDB STEM programs.[[0:12:21]] A testifier speaking about his water rights was told to stop.[[1:04:44]] The Maui Farm, which offers transitional housing to families facing homelessness, asked for $323,000.[[1:22:01]] A testifier said deer are destroying pastures and farmland.[[1:29:23]] A family-support coalition said it was left out of the mayor's proposed budget for fiscal year 27.[[1:44:44]] A Farm Bureau speaker said the Farm Bureau and four commodity groups are asking for $564,000.[[1:54:54]] The meeting was adjourned after the last testifier.[[1:57:07]]
meeting.next: The chair said she will advocate for the Maui County Farm Bureau to be added to the budget. The family-support coalition said it will follow up with a budget summary. The chair said staff took notes and the committee will receive a summary of the testimony.

issues.oneLine: The Maui Farm asked for $323,000 in county funding for its transitional housing program.
issues.brief: The director said eight mothers and 15 children currently live on the farm.[[#1]] The director said the county grant makes up one-third of the farm's overall budget.[[#2]] The director said the request includes a $43,000 increase to cover rising costs.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: A testifier asked for county support for farmers and ranchers because deer are destroying pastures and farmland.
issues.why: A ranching group leader said Maui ranchers have cut their herds by over 50 percent because deer compete for grass.
issues.brief: A farmer said on-farm composting helps both waste diversion and food security.[[#1]] The ranching group leader said local calves are now kept and processed on Maui to feed residents.[[#2]]
